summary: Count to 100 by ones, fives and tens; count backward from 10.
Count forward starting from any given number, not just 1.
Write numbers 0 to 20 and use a numeral to show how many objects.
Recognize, extend and create repeating patterns with objects; name the repeating unit and rule.
Count objects 1-20 one-to-one; last number is how many; next is one more, previous one less.
Count up to 20 objects in a line, array or circle (10 scattered); count out a given number.
Say whether one group of objects has more than, fewer than, or the same as another.
Compare two written numbers up to 10 using greater than, less than, equal to.
Show adding and taking away with objects, fingers, drawings, sounds, acting out or equations.
Solve add-to, take-from and put-together problems within 10 using objects, drawings or equations.
Break numbers up to 10 into pairs in more than one way and record them.
Find the number that makes 10 with a given number from 1 to 9.
Use mental strategies to build fluency adding and subtracting within 10 (CCSS: within 5).
Show numbers 11 to 19 as ten ones and some more ones.
Describe things about an object that can be measured, like length or weight.
Directly compare two objects to see which has more or less of an attribute.
Identify penny, nickel, dime and quarter by size and color and know each value.
Sort objects into given categories of 10 or fewer and compare category sizes.
Name shapes around you and describe positions with words like above, below, beside, behind.
Name shapes correctly whatever their size or orientation.
Tell whether a shape is flat (two-dimensional) or solid (three-dimensional).
Compare 2-D and 3-D shapes by sides, corners and other features in informal language.
Build and draw shapes found in the world.
Make a figure from simple shapes and find smaller shapes inside a figure.
Solve add and subtract word problems within 20 with the unknown in any position.
Solve word problems adding three whole numbers with a sum up to 20.
Use identity, commutative and associative properties as strategies to add and subtract.
Treat subtraction as finding a missing addend.
Add and subtract within 20 with strategies: counting on or back, making ten, related facts.
Build fluency within 20 with mental strategies; know all sums and differences to 10.
Understand the equal sign and decide if addition and subtraction equations are true or false.
Find the missing whole number in an addition or subtraction equation.
Count to 120 by ones, twos and fives; count back from 20; read and write numbers to 120.
Extend counting patterns by ones, twos, fives and tens to predict the next number up to 120.
Know two-digit numbers are tens and ones, shown in several ways (39 = 2 tens 19 ones).
Compare two two-digit numbers using tens and ones and the symbols >, =, <.
Add a two-digit number and a one-digit number or a multiple of ten within 100; explain.
Mentally find 10 more or 10 less than a two-digit number.
Subtract multiples of 10 from any number 10-99 using models and place value strategies.
Order three objects by length and compare two lengths using a third object.
Measure length with non-standard units like paper clips and give a whole number of units.
Tell and write time to the hour and half hour on analog and digital clocks.
Count the value of a set of like coins under one dollar, using the cent sign.
Show and read data with up to three categories in pictographs, bar graphs and tally charts.
Tell defining from non-defining attributes of shapes; build and draw shapes with given attributes.
Combine 2-D or 3-D shapes to make composite shapes and new shapes from them.
Split circles and rectangles into halves and fourths and name the shares.
Solve one- and two-step add and subtract word problems within 100.
Fluently add and subtract within 30 mentally; know single-digit sums and related subtraction facts.
Decide if a group up to 20 is odd or even; write even numbers as doubles.
Use repeated addition to find the total in arrays up to 5 by 5.
Find patterns in an addition or hundreds chart and explain them with properties of operations.
Know three-digit numbers are hundreds, tens and ones and can be shown in several ways.
Extend counting patterns by ones, twos, fives, tens and hundreds to 1000.
Read and write numbers to 1000 in numerals, words and expanded form.
Compare two three-digit numbers using place value and >, =, <.
Add and subtract within 100 fluently using place value strategies.
Add up to four two-digit numbers using place value and properties.
Add and subtract within 1000 with models and place value and explain the reasoning.
Mentally add or subtract 10 or 100 to or from any number within 1000.
Measure length with tools like rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks and tapes.
Measure one object with two different units and relate the results to unit size.
Estimate lengths in inches, feet, yards, centimeters and meters.
Measure how much longer one object is than another in standard units.
Solve add and subtract word problems within 100 about lengths.
Show whole numbers, sums and differences within 100 on a number line.
Tell and write time to quarter hours and nearest five minutes, with a.m. and p.m.
Solve problems with coins under a dollar (cent sign) and whole dollars up to $100.
Make a line plot in whole-number units from a given data set.
Draw pictographs with keys of 1, 2, 5 or 10 and bar graphs; solve problems from them.
Identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons; draw 2-D shapes with given angles or equal sides.
Split a rectangle into rows and columns of equal squares and count them.
Split circles and rectangles into halves, thirds or fourths; equal shares can differ in shape.
Understand multiplication as the total in a number of equal groups.
Understand division as sharing into equal groups or finding the number of groups.
Solve multiplication and division word problems within 100 with groups, arrays and measures.
Find the missing number in a multiplication or division equation.
Use commutative, associative and distributive properties to multiply and divide.
Treat division as finding an unknown factor.
Multiply and divide within 100 fluently; know single-digit products from memory.
Solve two-step word problems with all four operations and check answers by estimating.
Find patterns in the multiplication chart and explain them with properties of operations.
Round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100 and explain on a number line.
Add and subtract within 1000 fluently.
Multiply one-digit numbers by multiples of 10 such as 9 x 80.
Read and write whole numbers up to 100,000 in standard, word and expanded form.
Understand unit fractions 1/b and fractions a/b as a parts of size 1/b.
Place fractions on a number line by splitting 0 to 1 into equal parts.
Find simple equivalent fractions, write whole numbers as fractions, compare like fractions.
Tell time to the minute and solve word problems about elapsed minutes.
Solve money problems: coins under a dollar with cent sign, whole dollars up to $1000.
Measure mass and liquid volume in g, kg, mL, L and estimate with benchmarks (no word problems).
Draw scaled picture and bar graphs and solve how-many-more problems from them.
Measure lengths to half and quarter inches and show data on a line plot.
Understand area as covering a shape with unit squares.
Find area by counting unit squares.
Connect area to multiplication and addition, including rectangles split into parts.
Solve perimeter problems, including missing sides and same perimeter with different areas.
Know shapes share attributes; recognize rhombuses, rectangles and squares as quadrilaterals.
Split shapes into equal-area parts named as unit fractions; equal shares need not match in shape.
Decide whether a figure is a polygon.
Read a multiplication equation as a comparison, such as 35 is 5 times 7.
Multiply or divide to solve word problems about multiplicative comparison.
Solve multi-step whole-number word problems, interpret remainders, write equations (no estimation check).
Find factor pairs to 100, multiples, and decide if a number is prime or composite.
Make a number or shape pattern from a rule and describe its features.
Know each place is ten times the place to its right.
Read, write and compare multi-digit whole numbers in several forms.
Round whole numbers to any place up to hundred thousands and explain on a number line.
Fluently add and subtract within 1,000,000 using efficient strategies and algorithms.
Multiply up to four digits by one digit and two digits by two digits.
Divide up to four-digit numbers by one-digit numbers, with remainders.
Explain and generate equivalent fractions by multiplying top and bottom by the same number.
Compare fractions with different numerators and denominators.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with like denominators, including word problems.
Multiply a fraction by a whole number, including word problems.
Rewrite tenths as hundredths and add tenths and hundredths.
Write tenths and hundredths as decimals and place them on a number line.
Compare decimals to hundredths.
Measure and estimate to learn relative sizes of customary and metric units (conversion moved to grade 5).
Solve one- or two-step whole-number measurement problems in one system, without unit conversions.
Use area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in problems.
Make line plots of fraction measurements and solve problems from them.
Understand angles and degree measure as parts of a circle.
Measure and sketch angles with a protractor.
Add angle measures and find unknown angles.
Draw and identify points, lines, rays, segments, angles incl. straight and reflex, parallel and perpendicular lines.
Classify 2-D figures by parallel or perpendicular sides and angles; classify triangles as right, acute, obtuse.
Find and draw lines of symmetry.
Evaluate whole-number expressions with parentheses or brackets using order of operations (no exponents).
Write simple expressions and interpret them without evaluating.
Make two number patterns from rules, relate terms and graph them as ordered pairs.
Know each place is ten times the place to its right and one tenth of its left.
Explain patterns when multiplying or dividing by powers of 10; use exponents for powers of 10.
Read, write and compare decimals to thousandths.
Round decimals to the nearest hundredth, tenth or whole number and explain on a number line.
Fluently multiply whole numbers up to three digits by four digits.
Divide up to four-digit numbers by two-digit numbers, with remainders.
Add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals to hundredths.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with unlike denominators.
Solve fraction add and subtract word problems and check reasonableness with benchmarks.
Understand a fraction as division and solve sharing problems with fraction answers.
Multiply fractions by whole numbers and fractions, including area with fractional sides.
Understand multiplying as scaling: predict product size from the factor.
Solve real-world problems multiplying fractions and mixed numbers.
Divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions; problems also use non-unit fractions.
Convert larger units to smaller within one system and solve multi-step measurement problems with them.
Make line plots of fraction measurements and solve problems with them.
Understand volume as filling a solid with unit cubes.
Find volume by counting unit cubes.
Find volumes of rectangular prisms with formulas and add volumes of combined prisms.
Graph and label ordered pairs in the first quadrant; know what each coordinate means.
Graph points in the first quadrant to solve problems.
Classify 2-D figures in a hierarchy; attributes of a category belong to its subcategories.

state_code: # - Tennessee Math Standards (State Board of Education approved Feb 5, 2021; implemented 2023-24; in effect until revised standards in 2031-32):
# - Official crosswalk (2017 TN standards to the 2023-implemented TN standards; it does not map to CCSS):
# - No official TN-to-CCSS crosswalk was found; CCSS links here are judged from the standard text.
# - Grade.Domain.Cluster.Standard (e.g. K.MD.B.3). Domains and clusters look like CCSS, but numbers often differ from CCSS for the same
#   content: K.CC is renumbered after the new pattern standard (TN K.CC.B.5 = CCSS K.CC.B.4), TN K.MD.B.3 is coins (CCSS K.MD.B.3 is sorting),
#   1.NBT is shifted by one (TN 1.NBT.B.3 = CCSS 1.NBT.B.2), 1.MD.C.5 = CCSS 1.MD.C.4. Never assume a TN code means the same-coded CCSS standard.
# - Lettered sub-parts restating CCSS sub-parts are folded. 3.MD.A.1 is split into 3.MD.A.1a (time) and 3.MD.A.1b (money) as in the TN crosswalk.
# - None dropped as a whole. Merged: CCSS 1.OA.C.5 into TN 1.OA.C.5; 2.NBT.B.9 into TN 2.NBT.B.7; 5.G.B.4 into TN 5.G.B.3.
# - Parts dropped: 3.MD.A.2 one-step mass/volume word problems; 4.OA.A.3 estimation check; 4.MD.A.1 larger-to-smaller conversion and
#   conversion tables (moved to TN 5.MD.A.1); 2.G.A.1 cubes/faces; 2.MD.D.9 measuring to generate the data; size limit of 10 in K.CC.C.6.
# - New: repeating patterns in K (K.CC.A.4); polygon or not (3.G.A.3).
# - Earlier than CCSS: coins in K and grade 1 (K.MD.B.3, 1.MD.B.4); money to $1000 in grade 3 (3.MD.A.1b); skip-count patterns in grade 1 (1.NBT.A.2);
#   addition/hundreds-chart patterns in grade 2 (2.OA.D.5); numbers to 100,000 in grade 3 (3.NBT.A.4); fluency within 10 in K (K.OA.A.5).
# - Beyond CCSS inside matched standards: fluency within 30 in grade 2 (2.OA.B.2); counting by 5s and backward in K and grade 1; pictograph keys
#   of 2, 5, 10 in grade 2; straight/reflex angles and triangle classification by angles in grade 4; whole dollars to $100 in grade 2.
# - The PDF linked as current is marked "Revised November 6, 2020" (the version the SBE approved in Feb 2021); crosswalk revised April 2022 matches it.
# - K.OA.A.5 also lists 1.OA.C.6 because TN expects fluency within 10 in K. 5.MD.A.1 also lists 4.MD.A.1 and 4.MD.A.2 (conversions and
#   measurement problems that CCSS puts in grade 4).
# - 1.NBT.A.2 marked moved to 2.NBT.A.2 (skip-counting patterns); 2.OA.D.5 marked moved to 3.OA.D.9 (arithmetic patterns in tables).
# - 3.MD.A.1b mapped to 2.MD.C.8 (money word problems, no decimal notation required); it is a grade-3 extension of that content.
# - kind is judged on content: same = CCSS content with only rewording, examples or limits that CCSS also implies.
